chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Imran al-Halabi, who said:

I heard Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام saying, and he was asked about a man who prays the Jumu'ah prayer as four rak'ahs: should he recite aloud in it? He said: Yes, and the qunut is in the second rak'ah.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ: a four-rak'ah form of the prayer
key_terms.الْقُنُوتُ: the supplicatory raising of the hands in prayer
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةِ: the Qur'anic recitation within the prayer

ai.seo_question: Should a person praying Jumu'ah as four rak'ahs recite aloud and perform qunut?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who performs the Jumu'ah prayer as four rak'ahs, such as when praying individually or while traveling. It states that the recitation is to be done aloud and that the qunut is performed in the second rak'ah.
